policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 9:1 reads 'And he entered into a boat' with a bare pronoun; the added subject ὁ Ἰησοῦς would surface as 'Jesus', which the ASV does not print here.
ASV 9:1 reads 'into a boat', indefinite; the articular εἰς τὸ πλοῖον would give 'the boat' in the ASV's article-sensitive practice.
ἀφίενταί and ἀφέωνταί are the same verb in different tense-forms and both yield ASV 'thy sins are forgiven'; no note is mapped here (the only note is a greek_gloss on 'Son').
ASV 9:2 reads 'thy sins are forgiven' with a single possessive and no dative; the RP reading adds σοι, which the ASV would render 'thee' as it does elsewhere for a dative of advantage.
ASV 9:4 reads 'Jesus knowing their thoughts' = εἰδὼς, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read seeing' places ἰδὼν in the margin, confirming the text follows εἰδὼς.
ASV 'Wherefore think ye evil' carries its subject in the verb; an added emphatic ὑμεῖς is not separately representable in English and the mapped note concerns εἰδὼς/ἰδὼν, not this unit.
Ἀφίενταί and Ἀφέωνταί are alternative forms of the same verb, both rendered 'Thy sins are forgiven'; the ASV wording does not distinguish them and no note is attached.
Ἔγειρε and Ἔγειραι are alternative imperative forms of the same verb, both giving ASV 'Arise'; nothing in the English or the notes selects one.

ASV 'Arise, and take up thy bed' is equally the ASV's habitual coordination of a circumstantial participle (Ἐγερθεὶς) and a plain second imperative (Ἔγειρε); the English cannot tell them apart and no note is mapped.
ASV 9:8 reads 'they were afraid' = ἐφοβήθησαν; ἐθαύμασαν would give 'they marvelled', a different English word the ASV does not print.
ASV 9:10 opens 'And it came to pass', rendering the conjunction; the omission would leave the clause without the initial 'And'.
ἔλεγον (imperfect) and εἶπον (aorist) are both rendered 'they said' in ASV 9:11; the English does not distinguish the tenses and the only note points to 5:46.
ASV 9:12 reads 'But when he heard it, he said' with a pronoun subject; the added Ἰησοῦς would appear as 'Jesus', which the ASV does not print here.
ASV 9:12 reads simply 'he said, They that are whole'; the added αὐτοῖς would give 'said unto them', absent from the ASV.
ASV 9:13 ends 'but sinners.' with nothing further; the RP addition εἰς μετάνοιαν would give 'to repentance', which the ASV does not print.
ASV 9:14 reads 'fast oft', rendering πολλά, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit oft' places the omission in the margin.
ASV 9:17 reads 'the skins perish' in the present, matching ἀπόλλυνται alongside the present 'burst' and 'is spilled'; the future ἀπολοῦνται would give 'will perish'.

ASV 9:18 'there came a ruler, and worshipped him' renders the participle without a separate complement; 'there came' serves the simplex ἐλθὼν and the compound προσελθὼν alike, and no note is mapped to this unit.
ἠκολούθει (imperfect) and ἠκολούθησεν (aorist) are both rendered 'followed him' in ASV 9:19; the English does not mark the aspectual difference and no note is attached.
στραφεὶς and ἐπιστραφεὶς both yield ASV 'turning'; the two notes here are classed alternative_rendering and concern 'made thee whole', so they cannot decide a reading.
ASV 9:24 reads 'he said, Give place' with no indirect object; the RP reading λέγει αὐτοῖς would give 'he saith unto them', absent from the ASV.
ASV 9:27 reads 'two blind men followed him', rendering the dative αὐτῷ; the omission would leave the verb without the expressed object.
ASV 9:27 'thou son of David' is direct address, which renders the vocative υἱὲ and the nominative-for-vocative υἱὸς identically; no note is mapped.
ἐνεβριμήθη and ἐνεβριμήσατο are alternative aorist forms of one verb, both giving ASV 'strictly charged them'; the sole note ('Or, sternly') is an alternative_rendering about English wording.

ASV 9:32 'a dumb man possessed with a demon' is the natural English for substantival κωφόν standing alone as much as for ἄνθρωπον κωφόν; 'man' does not prove the noun was in the text, and no note is mapped.
ASV 9:35 ends 'all manner of sickness.'; the RP addition ἐν τῷ λαῷ would give 'among the people', which the ASV does not print.
ὡσεὶ and ὡς are both rendered 'as' in ASV 9:36 'as sheep not having a shepherd'; the English does not distinguish the particles and no note is attached.
